item.question_text: A firm assembles a fraud-detection service: a partner supplies the training data, a vendor supplies the model, and the firm then licenses the finished service to banks. Applying the Annex A control on allocating responsibilities, what does the firm have to do?

options.text: Apportion life cycle duties among itself, the partner, the vendor, the banks and other outside parties.
Record each party taking part in the life cycle together with the duties settled for them.
Draw the boundaries of its management system so that the outsourced stages fall inside them.
Capture the banks' stated expectations for the service and carry them into design requirements.

item.explanation: The Annex A control on allocating responsibilities is expressed as a requirement covering the whole life cycle and reaching beyond the organization itself: responsibilities are 'allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties' (A.10.2). The other options describe Annex B implementation guidance or a different clause on scope.
item.key_support: The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.

distractor_support.support: The organization should document all parties intervening in the AI system life cycle and their roles and determine their responsibilities.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Documenting the parties is implementation guidance phrased as 'should', not the required action of the control.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall determine the boundaries and applicability of the AI management system to establish its scope.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Setting scope boundaries is a separate obligation and does not discharge the allocation of life cycle responsibilities.

distractor_support.support: The organization should ensure that its responsible approach to the development and use of AI systems considers their customer expectations and needs.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Considering customer expectations is guidance about customers, not the allocation of responsibilities across life cycle parties.

item.question_text: An organization is setting up accountability for its AI work and asks what should govern how its internal AI roles and duties are shaped. Which statement reflects the Annex A control on AI roles and responsibilities?

options.text: Roles and duties for AI are set and assigned in line with what the organization needs.
Roles and duties for AI mirror the role categories described in the AI vocabulary standard.
Roles and duties for AI follow the split of work written into the organization's customer contracts.
Roles and duties for AI are assigned after the management system scope has been issued.

item.explanation: A.3.2 makes definition and allocation of AI roles a requirement whose shape is driven by the organization: 'Roles and responsibilities for AI shall be defined and allocated according to the needs of the organization.' The other options substitute an external taxonomy, contracts or a sequencing rule that the control does not state.
item.key_support: Roles and responsibilities for AI shall be defined and allocated according to the needs of the organization.

distractor_support.support: A detailed description of these roles is provided by ISO/IEC 22989.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The referenced role descriptions are informative background, not the basis prescribed for allocating roles.

distractor_support.support: 2) contractual obligations;
distractor_support.why_wrong: Contractual obligations are one internal context consideration, not the stated basis for defining and allocating AI roles.

distractor_support.support: The scope shall be available as documented information.
distractor_support.why_wrong: No sequencing that ties role allocation to publication of the scope document is stated.

item.question_text: An AI management system lead argues that responsibility allocation for the organization's AI system stops at its own employees. Why is this reading of the responsibility-allocation control mistaken?

options.text: Because the allocation runs across the organization together with its partners, suppliers, customers and outside parties.
Because anyone who perceives themselves to be affected by the activity takes a share of the duties.
Because the duties for the AI system are apportioned by the customer that receives the product.
Because the duties for the AI system are transferred to the supplier providing the models and data.

item.explanation: A.10.2 requires responsibilities in the AI system life cycle to be allocated 'between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties', so the allocation deliberately extends past internal staff. The alternatives invent a different allocating actor or a wholesale transfer of duties.
item.key_support: The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.

distractor_support.support: that can affect, be affected by, or perceive itself to be affected by a decision or activity
distractor_support.why_wrong: Being an interested party describes who may be affected, not who is allocated life cycle responsibilities.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The organization, not the customer, is the actor required to ensure the allocation is made.

distractor_support.support: In an AI system life cycle, responsibilities can be split between parties providing data, parties providing algorithms and models, parties developing or using the AI system and being accountable with regard to some or all interested parties.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Responsibilities are split among the parties involved rather than handed over wholesale to the supplier.

item.question_text: A retailer contracts an external laboratory to test and validate its AI model before release. What follows for the retailer from the control on allocating responsibilities across the AI system life cycle?

options.text: Responsibility for the testing stage is apportioned between the retailer and the laboratory.
Responsibility for the testing stage passes to the laboratory once the contract is signed.
The testing stage sits outside the retailer's allocation while the work is performed externally.
The retailer captures the laboratory's expectations as a supplier of the testing service.

item.explanation: A.10.2 requires responsibilities within the AI system life cycle to be allocated between the organization and third parties, so engaging an external tester is precisely a case where the split has to be settled rather than avoided.
item.key_support: The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.

distractor_support.support: The organization should document all parties intervening in the AI system life cycle and their roles and determine their responsibilities.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The guidance points to determining each party's responsibilities, not to a contract transferring the organization's responsibilities away.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Externally performed life cycle activities are exactly what the allocation across third parties covers.

distractor_support.support: The organization should understand customer expectations and needs when it is supplying a product or service related to an AI system (i.e. when it is itself a supplier).
distractor_support.why_wrong: Understanding expectations applies when the organization is the supplier to a customer, which is not the situation described.

item.question_text: An organization treats the Annex A control on allocating AI life cycle responsibilities and the Annex B implementation guidance on recording the parties involved as carrying identical weight. Which description of their status is accurate?

options.text: Allocating the responsibilities is stated as a requirement; recording the parties is offered as guidance.
Recording the parties is stated as a requirement; allocating the responsibilities is offered as guidance.
Both are set out as requirements applying to the organization's AI system life cycle.
Both are offered as guidance the organization considers when it splits life cycle duties.

item.explanation: The Annex A control is written with 'shall' — 'The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties' (A.10.2) — whereas the Annex B implementation guidance on documenting the parties is written with 'should'.
item.key_support: The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.

distractor_support.support: The organization should document all parties intervening in the AI system life cycle and their roles and determine their responsibilities.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The statuses are reversed: documenting the parties is 'should' guidance while the allocation control is 'shall'.

distractor_support.support: Control The organization should ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The Annex B text is phrased as guidance, so the two are not both requirements.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The allocation of responsibilities is mandatory wording, so treating both as advisory is incorrect.

item.question_text: A ten-person startup that deploys a single purchased AI tool argues that, because of its size, it need not define who is accountable for AI. Which response is correct?

options.text: AI roles and duties have to be defined and assigned, shaped by what the startup itself needs.
AI roles and duties are recommended at that size and their assignment can be deferred.
AI roles and duties have to be assigned once the startup supplies its tool to outside customers.
AI roles and duties have to be assigned by organizations that build models rather than deploy them.

item.explanation: A.3.2 states that 'Roles and responsibilities for AI shall be defined and allocated according to the needs of the organization' — the obligation stands, and it is the organization's needs that determine how the roles are shaped, not its size, its supply relationships or whether it builds models.
item.key_support: Roles and responsibilities for AI shall be defined and allocated according to the needs of the organization.

distractor_support.support: Roles and responsibilities for AI shall be defined and allocated according to the needs of the organization.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The control uses mandatory wording, so it is not an optional or deferrable recommendation.

distractor_support.support: Where the organization supplies an AI system to a third party, the organization should ensure that it takes a responsible approach to developing the AI system.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Supplying a system to a third party triggers separate guidance; it is not the trigger for defining AI roles.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall consider the intended purpose of the AI systems that are developed, provided or used by the organization.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Organizations that use AI systems are covered as well, so the obligation is not limited to developers.

item.question_text: A vendor tells a prospective customer that its management system certificate demonstrates that its AI systems satisfy the AI legislation applying to them. Regarding legal obligations, what does the AI management system standard actually place on the organization?

options.text: Top management establishes an AI policy that commits the organization to meeting applicable requirements.
A certification body attests that the organization meets the legal requirements applying to its AI systems.
A documented plan for notifying users of incidents is the required route to discharging legal obligations.
An information security management system is required wherever legal obligations touch AI system security.

item.explanation: The AI policy requirement in 5.2 obliges top management to make a commitment, stating that the policy "includes a commitment to meet applicable requirements" (5.2). That supports a claim of responsible, accountable management of legal obligations; it is not an attestation that the law has been satisfied, and nothing in the standard has a certifier confirm legal compliance.
item.key_support: includes a commitment to meet applicable requirements

distractor_support.support: The organization shall determine external and internal issues that are relevant to its purpose and that affect its ability to achieve the intended result(s) of its AI management system.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The standard places determination of legal and regulatory issues and the policy commitment on the organization itself, not an attestation of legal compliance on a certification body.

distractor_support.support: The organization should determine and document a plan for communicating incidents to users of the system.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Incident communication planning is expressed as should-level implementation guidance for a specific control, not as the standard's mechanism for meeting legal obligations.

distractor_support.support: If an organization identifies the need to implement an AI management system and to address security objectives in a similar thorough and systematic way, it can implement an information security management system in conformity with ISO/IEC 27001.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Integration with a security management system is presented as something the organization can do, not as an obligation arising from legal requirements.
